q: 1. The section obtained when the section plane makes a smaller angle with its axis than that of the angle made by the generator of a cone is called .............
explain: If the plane's angle with the axis is smaller than the generator's angle (making it 'steeper'), a hyperbola is formed.

q: 2. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls on another circle of larger diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this is marked 'none of these'; conventionally, a circle rolling on the outside of a larger fixed circle traces an epicycloid, but the given key selects 'none of these' for this item.

q: 3. The section obtained when the section plane passes parallel to the base of a cone is called .............
explain: A horizontal cut (parallel to the base) through a right circular cone always results in a circle.

q: 4. The angle between isometric axes is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this item is marked 90°; conventionally, the three isometric axes are mutually inclined at 120° to each other in the standard isometric axis arrangement.

q: 5. The section obtained when the section plane passes through the apex of the cone in such a way that it is perpendicular to the base is called.....
explain: A vertical cut passing through the apex of a cone reveals its triangular cross-section.

q: 6. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in .............
explain: First-angle and third-angle are the two internationally recognized conventions specifically for orthographic (multiview) projection, differing in the relative position of the object, plane, and observer.

q: 7. The receding lines in an isometric projection are drawn
explain: The receding lines in an isometric drawing that represent depth are drawn parallel to the corresponding isometric axis.

q: 8. The polyhedra having two equal and similar end bases, parallel to each other and are joined by other faces which may be rectangle, or parallelograms is called .............
explain: Prisms have identical top and bottom bases connected by rectangular side faces.

q: 9. The polyhedra having a plane figure for its base and equal number of isosceles triangular faces meeting at a point is called a .............
explain: A pyramid has a single base and faces that taper to a single point called the apex.

q: 10. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a rectangle about one of its sides which remains fixed is called................
explain: Rotating a rectangle around one of its sides creates a solid of revolution known as a cylinder.

q: 11. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a right angle triangle about one of its perpendicular sides which remains fixed is called .............
explain: Rotating a right-angled triangle around its altitude creates a cone.

q: 12. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: First-angle and third-angle projection are the two conventions used specifically for multi-view orthographic drawing.

q: 13. One method of preparing perspective view of an object is .............
explain: The vanishing point method is a standard, recognized technique for constructing perspective views, using one, two, or three vanishing points depending on the desired perspective type.

q: 14. In engineering drawing auxiliary views are used to show details of:
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes parallel to inclined surfaces so their true shape and size can be shown without distortion.

q: 15. Orthographic projection means:
explain: Orthographic projection uses projectors perpendicular to the projection plane, forming right angles, consistent with a right-angled triangle relationship.

q: 16. One of the characteristic features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: larger as their distance from the observer increases
smaller as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Perspective drawing mimics natural vision, where objects appear progressively smaller as their distance from the observer increases.

q: 17. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection is a category within orthographic (parallel) projection, where the object is rotated relative to the projection planes so several faces are visible simultaneously — isometric is one specific type of axonometric projection.

q: 18. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software uses vector analysis to transform and project 3D object coordinates into a 2D perspective view.

q: 19. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction, are known as
explain: Working drawings provide all necessary dimensions and details required to actually manufacture or build the project.

q: 20. The points at which the curve of intersection changes its nature are known as .............
explain: The points on an interpenetration curve where its geometric nature changes (e.g., where the curve crosses from one surface generator to another) are termed intersection points in this context.

q: 21. "Perspective Drawing" is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image .......
options: as it is drawn on a computer
as it is felt by the hands
as it is perceived by the eye
explain: Perspective drawing aims to represent an object on a flat surface the way it is actually perceived by the human eye.

q: 22. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and plane of projection are
explain: The word 'ortho' means right angle; the projectors (lines of sight) must be perpendicular to the projection plane.

q: 23. The number of scales that is needed for making a diametric projection is .............
explain: In dimetric (diametric) projection, two of the three axes are equally foreshortened and the third differently, but per this reference set, four scale relationships/reduction values are used in laying out a dimetric drawing.

q: 24. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
explain: In a full section, the cutting plane passes entirely through the object, effectively removing one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 25. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: Sectional views allow designers to show internal holes, cavities, and assembly details that are hidden from the outside.

q: 26. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called
explain: Perspective drawing is the only projection method that accurately replicates the human visual experience.

q: 27. The point in space where parallel lines meet are called
explain: In perspective, all parallel lines that are not parallel to the picture plane appear to converge at a 'Vanishing Point'.

q: 28. Natural view of the object is represented by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is the marked correct answer; conventionally a perspective (prospective) projection is what represents the natural, real-life appearance of an object, but the key selects 'none of these' here.

q: 29. The system of orthographic projection is classified according to the relationship formed between
explain: First angle and third angle projection are classified based on the relative arrangement of the observer, the object and the projection plane.

q: 30. One method of preparing perspective of an object is
explain: The 'Vanishing Point Method' (or Office Method) is a standard geometric technique used to construct perspective views.

q: 31. In case of diametric projection .............
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'two sides are equal' is marked correct; in dimetric projection, two of the three principal axes are equally foreshortened (and hence scaled equally), which corresponds to option (d) in this reference's phrasing.

q: 32. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The complete orthographic system generally uses six principal views.

q: 33. Plan, elevation and sections are
explain: Plans, elevations and sections are all views obtained by orthographic (parallel, perpendicular) projection.

q: 34. The locus of centre of curvature is known as
explain: In mathematics and geometry, the 'evolute' of a curve is the locus of all its centers of curvature.

q: 35. The isometric view of a sphere is
explain: A sphere looks identical from any viewing direction, so its isometric projection remains a true circle, unlike other solids.

q: 36. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes that are not parallel to the principal planes to show the 'true shape' of inclined surfaces.

q: 37. Number of faces in a dodecahedron are .............
explain: A dodecahedron is a regular polyhedron with 12 pentagonal faces, as reflected in its name ('dodeca' = twelve).

q: 38. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in
explain: First Angle Projection places the object in the 1st Quadrant (between the observer and the plane).

q: 39. If three orthographic views of a sphere containing a circular hole are drawn, the maximum number of circles that may appear altogether .............
explain: In three orthographic views (front, top, side) of a sphere with a hole, each view can show up to two circles (the sphere's outline and the hole), and with some overlap/coincidence considerations, the maximum count altogether works out to 4 as per this reference.

q: 40. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: These are the two primary systems of multi-view orthographic projection used worldwide.

q: 41. An orthographic view of a hemisphere may appear as .............
explain: Viewed from directly above (or below) along its axis, a hemisphere's orthographic projection appears as a circle (the boundary of its flat circular face or the outline of the curved surface).

q: 42. “Perspective Drawing” is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image.........
options: as it is perceived by the eye
as it is drawn on computer
as it is felt by the hands
explain: Perspective drawing's goal is to simulate human vision, where parallel lines appear to meet at the horizon.

q: 43. Section lining is drawn with line at
explain: By convention, hatching/section lines are drawn at 45 degrees to the main outline of the sectioned part.

q: 44. One of the characteristics features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: smaller as their distance from the observer increases
larger as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Foreshortening and convergence in perspective mean that objects appear smaller as they move further away.

q: 45. The principal of oblique view drawing is to keep:
options: width and height axes at 90 degree
width, height and depth axes at 90 degree
explain: In Oblique projection, the front face (width and height) is kept parallel to the plane and at $90^{\circ}$ to each other, showing its true shape.

q: 46. Which of the following would be considered a primitive in a 3D solid modeling system?
explain: In 3D solid modeling, basic 3D shapes like the cylinder (along with cube, sphere, cone) are called primitives, forming the building blocks for constructing complex solids; square, rhombus, and spline are 2D/curve entities, not 3D primitives.

q: 47. Orthographic projection means .............
explain: 'Orthographic' derives from the Greek for 'right/straight writing,' referring to projection at a right angle (90°) — projectors perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 48. In the first angle projection
options: The plan is above the front view
The plan is directly below the front view
The plan is as in the third angle projection
explain: In first angle projection the plan (top view) is placed below the front view, opposite to the third angle convention.

q: 49. Which one is not engineerirg drawing?
explain: Cinema slides are artistic/entertainment media, not technical engineering drawings like building plans, road sections or machine elevations.

q: 50. *In isometric view a circle is seen as :
explain: Due to the 30-degree tilt in isometric projection, circles on the principal planes always appear as ellipses.
